content.title: About
content.content: Corn squares are dry cereal made from whole corn, formed into small square pieces. They are crunchy, mildly sweet, and commonly enjoyed as a quick breakfast or snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn squares first appeared in the United States in the early 20th century as an alternative to wheat cereals.
The square shape is convenient for portion control and is often used in children's meals.
Their fiber content is higher than that of most traditional rice cereals.
The corn used is typically non‑GMO in European production.
Corn squares are frequently fortified with B‑vitamins and iron.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Corn squares provide sustained energy through slow release of glucose.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and helps maintain normal cholesterol levels.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many snack cereals, corn squares contain almost no fat.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and niacin aid metabolic processes.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Corn is naturally gluten‑free, making the product suitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Large portions can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar.

items.title: Added sugar content
items.content: Some varieties are sweetened, increasing their calorie count.

items.title: Possible PET residues
items.content: Packaging may involve PET, which can leave microscopic residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Corn squares can be eaten dry, added to milk, yogurt or kefir. They are often used in children's meals, as a base for granola bars, or as a crunchy element in salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a dry, cool place in an airtight container. For long‑term storage, keep in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent moisture.
